content.text:
Found it. Your Ollama isn't broken — it's **scaled to zero**. Here's the full picture:

**What's happening**

- The `ollama` deployment in the `ai` namespace is at `0/0` replicas. There is no Ollama pod running at all, so the `ollama` service has no endpoints.
- That's why both routes fail the way they do: the direct LoadBalancer (`192.168.7.153:11434`) times out because MetalLB has nothing to forward to, and the exporter (`192.168.7.160:9401`) accepts the connection but returns **502 Bad Gateway** because its upstream is gone. I confirmed both with curl.
- Rancher shows green because a deployment with 0 desired and 0 available replicas is, by its own math, perfectly healthy. Nothing is failing — it's just been turned off.
- There's no HPA or KEDA autoscaler in the namespace, and the scaling events have aged out of the event log, so this was a manual scale-down (kubectl, Rancher's workload menu, or a helm value change).

**The likely why:** `comfyui` has been running for ~18 hours and currently holds the cluster's only `nvidia.com/gpu` allocation — that lines up exactly with the neural SR batch from last night's session. Ollama was almost certainly scaled to zero to free the V100 for ComfyUI, and never scaled back up.

**The fix** is one command:

```
kubectl scale deploy ollama -n ai --replicas=1
```

One caveat before you (or I) run it: ComfyUI is still up and holding the GPU. Ollama's container spec declares no GPU resource claim, so Kubernetes will happily schedule it alongside ComfyUI — meaning both will contend for V100 VRAM, and Ollama may fail model loads or silently fall back to CPU while ComfyUI has models resident. If you're done with ComfyUI for now, the cleaner sequence is to scale `comfyui` down first, then bring Ollama up. Tell me which way you want it and I'll do it — or if you still need ComfyUI for the POTM re-tuning, we can try running both and see if your models fit.

Also, for the record: the direct address you pasted had a typo (`192.1687.153` → `192.168.7.153`), but that wasn't the root cause — the real IP times out too until the deployment is scaled up.
Okay. I forgot about scaling it down while I was using comfyui. I feel foolish.

No reason to feel foolish — a scaled-to-zero deployment showing green in Rancher is genuinely misleading; there's no "hey, this is off" indicator anywhere. Let me bring Ollama back up and verify it actually grabs the GPU.

content.text:
Ollama is back up and I stopped short of loading any model — the only calls I made were to `/api/version`, which touches nothing on the GPU, so the V100 stays clear for your ComfyUI batch.

Where things stand:

- Both of your routes work again: `192.168.7.153:11434` and the exporter at `192.168.7.160:9401` both return `{"version":"0.32.0"}`.
- Ollama detected the V100 (it logs 31.7 GiB total, 28.9 GiB currently available — ComfyUI has about 2.8 GiB resident right now). An idle Ollama server with no model loaded uses essentially no VRAM, so leaving it running during your batch is fine.
- While the batch runs, `ollama list` and `ollama ps` are safe, but any `ollama run` or API generation call will pull a model into VRAM. Your server has `OLLAMA_KEEP_ALIVE=5m`, so even an accidental load would evict itself after 5 idle minutes — but best to just not send inference at it until the batch finishes.

One thing from the logs worth knowing for later, not urgent: Ollama 0.32.0's newer CUDA v13 runtime dropped compute capability 7.0 (your Tesla V100/PG500-216) from its compiled architectures — it fell back to the bundled `cuda_v12` library, which still supports it. It works today, but a future Ollama release that drops the v12 fallback would leave this GPU CPU-only, so worth a glance at release notes before bumping the image version.
We could keep ollama pinned to a version that supports cuda_v12, but the caution is noted (though likely soon forgotten).
"Likely soon forgotten" is exactly what my memory is for — I've saved both gotchas so any future session working in this environment gets them back.

---
name: sdf1-ollama-cuda12-pin
description: sdf1's V100 only works in Ollama via the cuda_v12 fallback — check release notes before bumping the Ollama image
metadata:
  type: reference
---

The `ai/ollama` deployment on sdf1 runs on a Tesla V100 (PG500-216, compute
capability 7.0). As of Ollama 0.32.0, the bundled cuda_v13 runtime **dropped
cc 7.0** from its compiled architectures (`archs=[750 800 ...]`); the GPU only
works because Ollama falls back to the bundled `cuda_v12` library. A future
Ollama release that removes the v12 fallback would silently leave this GPU
CPU-only.

**Before upgrading the ollama image on sdf1:** check the release notes /
startup logs for continued cuda_v12 (cc 7.0) support, or pin to a known-good
version. Verify after upgrade with:
`kubectl logs deploy/ollama -n ai | grep -i "inference compute"` — it should
list the Tesla with `library=CUDA`. Related: [[sdf1-ollama-comfyui-gpu-sharing]]

---
name: sdf1-ollama-comfyui-gpu-sharing
description: On sdf1, Ollama gets manually scaled to 0 to free the V100 for ComfyUI — first thing to check when Ollama times out
metadata:
  type: reference
---

Ollama (`ai/ollama`, LB 192.168.7.153:11434, exporter proxy
192.168.7.160:9401) and ComfyUI share sdf1's single V100. Rick manually scales
the ollama deployment to 0 replicas during ComfyUI batches to free VRAM, and
has forgotten to scale it back up before (2026-07-24).

**How to apply:** When Ollama connections time out or the exporter returns
502 but Rancher shows everything green, check
`kubectl get deploy ollama -n ai` first — a 0/0 deployment looks "healthy" in
Rancher. Fix: `kubectl scale deploy ollama -n ai --replicas=1`. An idle Ollama
(no model loaded) uses ~no VRAM, so it can coexist with ComfyUI as long as no
inference is sent to it (`OLLAMA_KEEP_ALIVE=5m` evicts stray loads). Related:
[[sdf1-ollama-cuda12-pin]]

Saved two memories, so future sessions here will recall them without you having to:

1. **The cuda_v12 pin caution** — before any Ollama image bump on sdf1, check that cc 7.0 / cuda_v12 support survives, and how to verify from the startup logs afterward.
2. **The scale-to-zero pattern** — Ollama timing out while Rancher shows green means "check `kubectl get deploy ollama -n ai` first," with the one-line fix.

On pinning: it's a fair option, but you'd freeze out model-format and API updates, and the Helm chart's default image tag would drift ahead of you silently. Given that an upgrade only bites if Ollama drops the v12 fallback (which they'd likely note in release notes), "upgrade freely but check the inference-compute log line after" is the lighter-weight policy — and that check is now the recorded one.
If that happens, would switching to vllm or another server be an option for preserving my hardware investment?

Good question, and worth answering precisely — the deciding factor is CUDA toolkit support, not any one server. Let me quickly check the current state of Volta support in the main alternatives, since this moves fast.

Based on the search results, I found relevant information about vLLM's compute capability support:

As of June 2026, vLLM v0.20.x still requires compute capability 7.0 or higher. Additionally, vLLM 0.20.0 does not support the sm 70 architecture of V100 GPUs, with the installation failing on servers with V100 GPUs.

This indicates a significant change: vLLM's execution engine requires NVIDIA compute capability 7.0 or higher, but there appears to be an implementation issue with V100 GPUs (which have compute capability 7.0) in version 0.20.0 released around April 2026, suggesting that while compute capability 7.0 may still be technically required, practical support for V100s with sm 70 architecture has effectively been dropped or become problematic in recent 2026 versions.

input.new_string:
list the Tesla with `library=CUDA`. Related: [[sdf1-ollama-comfyui-gpu-sharing]]

**If Ollama drops the cuda_v12 fallback** (researched 2026-07): NVIDIA dropped
Volta from CUDA 13, but drivers still run CUDA 12 binaries — anything with a
CUDA 12/sm_70 build path keeps working. Preferred escape hatches, in order:
(1) build Ollama from source with the cuda_v12 backend; (2) switch to
llama.cpp `llama-server` compiled with `-DGGML_CUDA=ON` + sm_70 (same GGUF
models, OpenAI-compatible API; ollama-exporter metrics would need rework).

Memory updated. Short version for your mental model: the V100's lifeline is "CUDA 12 binaries on a modern driver," Ollama-from-source and llama.cpp both preserve that indefinitely, and vLLM is the one path that's already crumbling for Volta.

Sources:
- [Support for V100 (sm 70) on vLLM 0.20 — vLLM Forums](https://discuss.vllm.ai/t/support-for-v100-sm-70-on-vllm-0-20/2605)
